text: Implemented P4 structured workloads. Core now owns safe declared-output manifests and validation, InputCodec/ResultCodec contracts, worker release and operation identity, TaskInvocation, DurableResultHandle, WorkerEvent, and ResultEnvelope. Protocol owns four bounded canonical major-v1 schemas: scala-slurm.task-invocation, result-handle, worker-event, and result-envelope, including a byte-exact standard-library Python fixture. The new worker module provides target-side typed launch staging through Scheduler[IO], operation registry and effectful ScalaTask runtime, bounded managed input/output/scratch/progress capabilities, explicitly lower-assurance native context, bounded locked event append, atomic-last non-overwriting result publication, and retry safety default Unknown. Managed reattachment checks schema before parsing bytes, then identity/epoch/operation/release/output size+digest before ResultCodec decode. Python and R examples cover exit-only, declared-output, and structured modes; Python modes and golden generation were executed successfully. Fault tests cover missing/extra/size/digest outputs, malformed/oversized envelopes, stale epochs, wrong schemas/releases, task/codec failures, concurrent publication, path locality, and fixed launcher input non-leakage. Verification: checkFormatting passes; full repository 111/111 on Scala 3.3.8 and 111/111 on 3.8.4; cross-worker packageBin passes; mote doctor clean. Static production audit found no readAllBytes, unbounded Queue, serialized closure/Future/JVM graph/IO value, hidden process builder, or unsafe cast. Known boundary: worker distribution/registry assembly is site-owned; current P2 agent endpoint and ManagedController exit-only submission facade do not yet automatically assemble remote managed typed submission, and low-level RegisteredTaskSubmitter deliberately supplies neither managed idempotency nor automatic retry.
